headline: 29,000 jobs in September. Economists wanted 90,000.
summary: US employers added 29,000 jobs in September, down from 133,000 in August. Economists had expected 90,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2%. Wages grew 3% in a year, the smallest gain since 2021. Few are being laid off and few hired, so the jobless now wait more than six months on average. It is the last jobs report before the November 3 election.
cover_answer: Hardly anyone is hiring, and hardly anyone is firing.
table_question: Would you leave a safe job to hunt for a better one?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Every month the government counts how many new jobs there are. This month it counted 29,000, which is small for a country this big, like one scoop of sand on a whole beach. Most grown-ups kept the jobs they already have. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Six-year-olds count. One scoop, a whole beach, and everyone keeps their chair.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, and 29,000 is not. The scoop of sand on the beach is the anchor: small against big, something they can picture. Vygotsky's point is that the words go to the adult, so the script ends on the grown-ups having it. Expect "will you lose your job?" Answer straight; most people kept theirs.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: The government counts jobs every month. September added 29,000; August added 133,000. Companies aren't firing many people, but they aren't hiring either, so anyone who loses a job now waits six months to find one. Musical chairs, with no chairs added and none taken away.
8-12.why: Nobody fired, nobody hired, so the standing stay standing.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out chains of cause and effect, so the script hands them one: few firings, few hirings, longer waits for anyone out of work. Musical chairs is the mechanism, a game they know where the rules decide who sits. Expect "so is it good or bad?" Both: good if you have a chair, bad if you are standing.

13-17.script: Who does a slow month hurt most, the people with jobs or the people looking? Wages rose 3% in a year, the smallest since 2021; the jobless now average six months out of work. Second: it's the last jobs report before November 3. Does one month's number deserve that weight?
13-17.why: Secure workers, stuck jobseekers. Then the election.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: the people with jobs are mostly safe, and the people without one are stuck for months. The script asks which matters more, then adds the election, where one number gets more weight than it earns. Kuhn's point is that argument is practised. Expect "is Trump to blame?" The report doesn't say.

5-7.a: Companies are keeping the workers they have and not adding many. Most grown-ups still have their jobs.

8-12.q: Why does the government count jobs?
8-12.a: To see if the economy is growing: more jobs, more people earning.
No. It means 29,000 more jobs than in August. Few fired, few hired.

13-17.a: Nobody knows. It's the last report before November 3.
